Consumer Non-Cyclicals: Consumer Non-Cyclicals delivered a robust earnings expansion, with the sector posting an average annual earnings growth of about 34.6%, placing it tenth among fifteen SGX sectors for earnings growth. Revenue rose more modestly, averaging a 9.1% increase and earning a sixth place ranking in revenue growth. Within the group, [#VC2.SI]Olam Group Ltd[\#VC2.SI] led the earnings surge, while [#EB5.SI]First Resources Ltd[\#EB5.SI] generated the strongest revenue gain. The sector’s performance is further shaped by Singapore’s high per‑capita consumption of essential goods, a stable regulatory framework for food safety, and government initiatives that support local sourcing of staples, all of which uniquely bolster non‑cyclical demand. These market‑specific factors help translate the strong earnings momentum into steady top‑line growth.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector recorded an average annual earnings decline of 8.46% while its revenue grew by 13.75% over the past year. This earnings contraction places the sector 14th out of 15 sectors for earnings growth, whereas the revenue expansion ranks it third among all sectors. [#AWK.SI]Fuxing China Group Ltd[\#AWK.SI] delivered the strongest earnings increase in the group, and [#5HH.SI]Prospera Global Ltd[\#5HH.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. In Singapore, the sector’s performance is uniquely shaped by the heavy reliance on tourism‑driven retail demand, which can swing sharply with travel restrictions and visitor arrivals. Additionally, fluctuating exchange rates affect the cost of imported consumer goods, influencing both margins and sales volumes for local retailers. These market‑specific dynamics help explain why revenue can rise even as earnings fall.
Transportation & Logistics: Transportation & Logistics recorded modest earnings growth of 1.94% and revenue growth of 2.71% over the past year. The sector ranked 13th out of 15 in earnings growth and also 13th in revenue growth, indicating slower expansion compared with most other SGX sectors. [#R14.SI]Eneco Energy Ltd[\#R14.SI] delivered the strongest earnings increase within the group, while [#FQ7.SI]Salt Investments Ltd[\#FQ7.SI] posted the highest revenue rise. Growth in Singapore’s logistics landscape is shaped by the government's push to develop the port as a regional hub, which adds capacity but also creates short-term congestion that can limit throughput. Additionally, tighter customs clearance procedures and a tightening of driver work-hour regulations uniquely influence cost structures for local freight operators. These sector-specific dynamics temper the overall growth rates despite the positive performance of the leading firms.
Healthcare: The Healthcare sector posted a robust earnings expansion of 25.2% on average over the past year, while revenue rose modestly by 3.89%. Among fifteen SGX sectors, it ranks eleventh for earnings growth and tenth for revenue growth. [#FHH.SI]FHH[\#FHH.SI] recorded the strongest earnings acceleration within the sector, and [#8YY.SI]Embracing Future Holdings Ltd[\#8YY.SI] delivered the highest revenue increase. Growth has been uniquely supported by Singapore’s ageing population, expanding government subsidies for medical services, and a streamlined regulatory pathway for new medical devices, all of which have heightened demand for health‑care products and services.
Properties & Real Estate: The Properties & Real Estate sector posted an average annual earnings growth of about 89.4%, placing it third among fifteen sectors, while its average annual revenue growth of roughly 12.8% ranked fourth. This strong earnings expansion is driven in part by Singapore’s limited land pool and ongoing demand for both residential and commercial space, which amplify rental yields and property valuations. Government cooling measures that temper price surges also create a more stable environment for developers to focus on volume growth. Within the sector, [#5IC.SI][#5IC.SI]SING Holdings Ltd[\#5IC.SI][\#5IC.SI] led the pack, delivering the highest yearly earnings growth as well as the top revenue growth among its peers. These dynamics underscore the sector’s robust performance relative to the broader market.
Energy: The Energy sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 46.18% over the past year, while its average annual revenue grew 21.12% in the same period. It ranks seventh for earnings growth and tops the list for revenue growth among the fifteen sectors tracked on the SGX. [#JFQ.SI]JFQ[\#JFQ.SI] recorded the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, and [#TPED.SI]PTT Exploration Production PCL DRC[\#TPED.SI] delivered the strongest yearly revenue growth. Growth has been uniquely supported by Singapore's role as a regional bunkering hub, recent expansions of LNG import facilities, and government incentives that encourage offshore gas exploration and renewable‑energy projects, all of which boost domestic demand for energy services.
Utilities: Utilities delivered a striking earnings expansion, with the sector posting an average annual earnings growth of about 45 percent, placing it eighth among fifteen sectors for earnings growth. At the same time, average annual revenue fell roughly 5 percent, the weakest performance among all sectors and ranking fifteenth for revenue growth. The strongest earnings surge came from [#5GD.SI]Sunpower Group Ltd[\#5GD.SI], while [#BEH.SI]China International Holdings Ltd[\#BEH.SI] led the sector in revenue growth despite the overall decline. In Singapore, utilities are especially shaped by regulated tariff adjustments and the need to meet national renewable‑energy targets, which can boost profitability but also constrain top‑line expansion when demand growth is limited.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector posted a robust average annual earnings growth of 48.03% while its average annual revenue grew 10.69% over the past year. Among fifteen SGX sectors, it ranks sixth for earnings growth and fifth for revenue growth. [#CNE.SI]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE.SI] led the sector with the highest yearly earnings expansion, and [#42W.SI]Zixin Group Holdings Ltd[\#42W.SI] delivered the strongest revenue increase. Growth was bolstered by Singapore’s low inflation on essential goods, strong household savings that sustain demand for staple products, and continued government emphasis on early‑education and food security, which uniquely support consumer‑defensive businesses.
Financial Services: Over the past year the Financial Services sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 2.24% while its average annual revenue growth reached 7.97%. This earnings pace placed the sector 12th out of 15 sectors, whereas the revenue expansion ranked it 8th. [#I49.SI]IFS Capital Ltd[\#I49.SI] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration within the sector, and [#K6S.SI]Prudential PLC[\#K6S.SI] recorded the highest revenue growth. Growth was further shaped by Singapore’s evolving regulatory framework that encourages fintech innovation and by the city-state’s status as a regional wealth hub, which together boost demand for banking, insurance and asset‑management services. These sector‑specific dynamics help explain why revenue grew faster than earnings.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector posted a steep decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings growth of minus 110.75 percent, placing it at the bottom of the fifteen sectors. Despite the earnings contraction, revenue grew modestly by 3.53 percent, earning the sector the eleventh spot for revenue growth. [#9VW.SI][#9VW.SI]Spackman Entertainment Group Ltd[\#9VW.SI][\#9VW.SI] led the sector in both earnings and revenue growth, recording the highest yearly increases among its peers. In Singapore, the sector is uniquely affected by tight content‑licensing regulations and a recent reallocation of broadcast spectrum that has limited advertising income, while government incentives for local digital media production have created only modest new revenue opportunities. These sector‑specific dynamics help explain why earnings fell sharply even as revenue showed modest improvement.
Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector posted an extraordinary earnings surge, with an average annual earnings growth of roughly 1,027 percent, placing it first among the fifteen SGX sectors. Revenue expanded at a steadier pace of about 8.4 percent, earning the sector a seventh place ranking for revenue growth. Within the sector, [#KUO.SI]International Cement Group Ltd[\#KUO.SI] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration, while [#C8R.SI]Jiutian Chemical Group Ltd[\#C8R.SI] led the revenue gains. In Singapore, the sector’s performance is shaped by the country’s limited land availability, which drives demand for high-value construction materials, and by the government’s ongoing infrastructure upgrades that boost cement and chemical consumption.
Infrastructures: The Infrastructures sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 298.83%, placing it second among fifteen sectors, while its average annual revenue growth of 2.93% ranked twelfth. [#Z77.SI]Singapore Telecommunications Ltd[\#Z77.SI] led the sector with the strongest yearly earnings expansion, and [#S59.SI]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59.SI] delivered the highest yearly revenue increase. Growth in this sector is uniquely driven by Singapore's intensive government investment in transport and utility networks, the island's limited land prompting premium pricing for infrastructure services, and the push toward a smart‑city framework that fuels demand for advanced telecommunications and aviation engineering solutions. These local dynamics amplify earnings potential even as overall revenue growth remains modest compared with other sectors.
REIT: The REIT sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 38.39% while its average annual revenue grew by 4.56% over the past year. Among the fifteen SGX sectors, it ranked ninth for earnings growth and ninth for revenue growth, reflecting solid but not leading performance. [#M1GU.SI]Alpha Integrated REIT[\#M1GU.SI] led the sector with the highest earnings growth, and [#DCRU.SI]Digital Core REIT[\#DCRU.SI] delivered the strongest revenue expansion. Growth was supported by Singapore’s limited land supply, which intensifies demand for high‑quality, income‑generating properties, and by the steady inflow of foreign capital attracted to REITs under the country’s stable regulatory framework. Additionally, the surge in e‑commerce logistics and data‑centre demand created specific tailwinds for Singapore REITs.
Industrials: Industrials posted a striking earnings surge, with the sector’s average annual earnings growth reaching 68.47%, placing it fourth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue growth was modest, averaging 2.08% and ranking fourteenth, indicating that profit gains are outpacing top-line growth. The strongest earnings performer was [#5OC.SI]Koyo International Ltd[\#5OC.SI], while [#Y06.SI]Green Build Technology Ltd[\#Y06.SI] delivered the highest revenue increase. In Singapore, the sector benefits from ongoing government investment in port capacity and logistics infrastructure, as well as a rise in demand for advanced construction materials driven by urban redevelopment projects. These market-specific drivers help sustain the earnings momentum even as overall revenue growth remains limited.
Technology: Singapore’s Technology sector posted a striking earnings surge, with average annual earnings growth of about 52.5%, placing it fifth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at a steadier pace of roughly 15.0% year-over-year, earning the sector the second-best ranking for revenue growth. The strongest earnings performer was [#5AB.SI]Trek 2000 International Ltd[\#5AB.SI], while [#9MT.SI]MetaOptics Ltd[\#9MT.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. Growth has been amplified by Singapore’s aggressive push for digitalisation, including nationwide adoption of cashless payments and expanding data-center capacity to support cloud services. Additionally, the government’s targeted grants for semiconductor and photonics research have provided a catalyst that is largely unique to the technology segment.
